memories.memory: I lean fiscally conservative, but I support paying higher local taxes when the money is clearly tied to maintaining public infrastructure and essential services.

During a 2019 public-sector project, I pushed back when a politically appointed supervisor wanted staff to alter a neutral briefing, because I believe career civil servants should serve the law rather than a particular party.
I was raised in a churchgoing family, but by my early forties I had become more agnostic and now treat religious claims as personal matters rather than guides for public policy.
I support legal immigration and a path to citizenship for long-term residents, although I think border enforcement and consistent employment rules are necessary for the system to be fair.
I gave $250 in 2023 to a local campaign opposing a proposed charter change because I believed it would concentrate too much authority in the mayor's office.
I have become more supportive of nuclear power after seeing how difficult it is for public agencies to meet emissions goals using only wind and solar.
I oppose the death penalty because I do not trust any government, even a competent one, with an irreversible punishment when courts can make mistakes.
